post.description: Move a phone number from one org to another. Billing anchor clamp (TENANT-04, tightened): ``billing_next_charge_at`` is a per-number monthly billing anchor consumed by the ``charge_phone_numbers`` management command (see ``billing.services.charge_phone_number_monthly``), which charges a number's *current* organization once ``billing_next_charge_at`` has passed and then advances the anchor by another month. The original TENANT-04 ruling had a cross-org transfer unconditionally reset the anchor to "transfer time + 1 month", so the target org always started a fresh monthly cycle at the moment of transfer. That ruling is superseded: it opened a billing "ping-pong" loophole, since every transfer pushed the anchor a full month out -- bouncing a number between two orgs more often than monthly slid the anchor forever and the monthly fee was never charged. The current rule clamps the anchor instead of resetting it, so a transfer can only ever pull the anchor *closer* to now, never push it further out: new_anchor = max(now, min(existing_anchor, now + 1 month)) (existing_anchor is None) -> now + 1 month Effects: - A genuine transfer of a number with an anchor already due soon (or any time within the next month) keeps that existing charge schedule -- whoever holds the number when the fee comes due pays it, so total fees are unchanged for same-owner reorgs. This is intentionally *not* prorated: the source org is not refunded for the unused remainder of its last charged cycle, and the target is not charged immediately upon transfer. - An overdue anchor (in the past, e.g. the reconciliation command just hasn't run yet) clamps to "now", so the new holder is charged at the next reconciliation instead of inheriting an ever-sliding future date. - A number with no billing history (``billing_next_charge_at`` is None) has no existing anchor to clamp, so it falls back to "now + 1 month", same as the original ruling's fresh-cycle behavior. - Ping-pong transfers gain nothing: the clamp can only move the anchor earlier or leave it unchanged, never later, so hopping a number between orgs cannot delay the charge indefinitely.

List the active subaccounts under a Twilio parent account. The response carries SIDs and names only. Each subaccount's auth token is parked in a ``VoipSubaccountDiscovery`` row and referenced by ``discovery_id``; ``VoipTwilioSubaccountConnectView`` reads it back from there so tokens never round-trip through the browser.

Create one ordinary Twilio connection per chosen subaccount. Every SID is handled on its own — its own verification evidence, trunk, connection row and transaction — so one bad subaccount reports ``failed`` without touching the others, and the discovery row stays valid until it expires so the failed SID can simply be sent again.

post.description: Hands the browser the connection's own access token for the Google Picker. Under `drive.file` the server has no grant on a spreadsheet until the user picks it, and the grant is recorded against the credential that ran the Picker session. Minting the token from this connection — rather than a separate browser-side token client — guarantees the picked-file grant lands on the very refresh token the tool executor later uses, instead of relying on grants being project-scoped across our per-environment OAuth clients. The token is short-lived and belongs to the grant this org admin already established, so handing it back to that same admin's browser exposes nothing they cannot already reach. It stays narrow only because the Sheets flow omits `include_granted_scopes` — with it, this token would union in every other scope the account granted this client. Keep that off.

typing_sound.description:

tool_start_line.description:
What the agent says when a tool call starts. always: a line at every tool call. only_if_slow: a line only if the tool is still running after a short wait. never: nothing at tool start.

* `always` - Always
* `only_if_slow` - Only if slow
* `never` - Never

send_email_enabled.description: Whether the agent may send an email to the configured recipient during a call.

send_sms_enabled.description: Whether the agent may send SMS through a customer-connected carrier number.

sms_allow_other_recipients.description: Whether the send_sms tool may text a recipient other than the current telephone party.

warm_transfer_style.description:
What happens when a warm transfer is answered. introduce (default): the caller is connected as soon as the person answers, then the AI introduces the caller on the line, which both hear, and leaves. ask_first: the caller waits on hold while the AI privately asks the person who answers whether they can take the call; they can decline. On yes the caller is connected and the AI introduces them on the line. whisper: the caller waits on hold while the AI privately tells the person who answers who is calling and why, without asking; then the caller is connected and the AI leaves with nothing said on the line.

* `introduce` - Introduce on the line
* `ask_first` - Ask first
